question_text: A 42-year-old woman presents because of a painful mass she first noticed on her neck 1 week ago (see image). The mass has grown over the last few days. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. On physical exam, her temperature is 38.0°C (100.4°F), pulse is 86/min, respirations are 12/min, blood pressure is 135/80 mm Hg. The mass is tender and relatively soft and mobile. The overlying skin is warm. On her right ear, there is a series of small and healing skin punctures left by the bite of her neighbor’s kitten 3 weeks ago. No other mass is detected in the neck, supraclavicular, axillary, or inguinal regions. Oral examination reveals several discolored teeth. Her lungs are clear to auscultation and heart sounds are normal. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic study at this time?
